documents.title: Generative AI Guidelines for MSU
documents.summary: ITS guidelines for generative AI at MSU that focus on data security: only public data goes into AI tools, expect training on inputs, and confidential data needs vetted, contracted tools. It says nothing about coursework.
documents.stance_why: The guidelines allow generative AI use but set conditions: "Only publicly available information ... may be used" and confidential data requires tools that "Must ... have undergone a comprehensive security risk review". It neither bans nor promotes AI, and does not hand coursework decisions to instructors, so permit with conditions.

units.why: The opening sentence frames the document as "general guidelines for the responsible use of generative AI", an institution-level framework, so P56 with actor all, phase general, informs.
units.anchor: general guidelines for the responsible use of generative AI at Mississippi State University

units.why: "should be viewed as posting data on a public website" is advice about data privacy to all users, so P50 (protect data), should.
units.anchor: AI tools and services should be viewed as posting data on a public website

units.why: "Only publicly available information ... may be used" limits what data can go into AI tools, a data-protection rule, so P50; modality is may because the text says "may be used", with the restriction carried by "Only".
units.anchor: may be used in generative AI tools and services
units.policy: Only publicly available information may be used in generative AI tools and services.

units.why: "Users should expect these AI tools and services to use input data for its training" is a warning about data retention and training use, so P50 and informs.
units.anchor: expect these AI tools and services to use input data for its training

units.why: Where source information requires authentication, "permission from the respective division VP may be needed" before putting it into AI tools; this is a data-protection approval step, so P50.
units.anchor: permission from the respective division VP may be needed
units.frag_start: If students, faculty, staff, or affiliates
units.frag_end: information in AI tools and services

units.why: "Generative AI should be used in accordance with the existing university policies (OP 01.12)" ties AI use to a university-wide framework, so P56 with should.
units.anchor: Generative AI should be used in accordance with the existing university policies

units.why: "Understand if informed consent and approval of the data subjects is required" asks users to consider data subjects before using AI, a privacy duty, so P50 and should.
units.anchor: Understand if informed consent and approval of the data subjects is required.

units.why: Users with proprietary or confidential information "Must use products or services that have undergone a comprehensive security risk review", which is the prefer-vetted-tools rule of P50, with must.
units.anchor: Must use products or services that have undergone a comprehensive security risk review

units.why: "Must use products or services that have a university contract in place" requires contracted tools for confidential data, so P50 (vetted or licensed tools) rather than P65, which concerns institutional review of AI contracts; must.
units.anchor: Must use products or services that have a university contract in place
units.frag_start: Must use products or services that have a university contract

documents.unit: CITE (Center for Instructional Technology and Excellence)
documents.title: Suggested MSU Generative AI Syllabus Statements
documents.summary: CITE offers three suggested syllabus statements ranging from open to strict AI use. Open and moderate options require citation and an acknowledgement statement; moderate and strict allow AI-detection review leading to the Honor Code Council.
documents.stance_why: The document gives instructors a choice of three templates ("Option 1: Open Use", "Option 2: Moderate Use", "Option 3: Strict Use") and sets no one rule itself, so by the codebook tiers/templates mean delegates.

units.why: The document lists three suggested syllabus statements (open, moderate, strict), i.e. named tiers that instructors pick from, so P05; it sets no single rule, so it is a neutral offering.
units.anchor: Suggested Mississippi State University Generative AI Syllabus Statements
units.policy: Three suggested syllabus statements are offered: Option 1 Open Use, Option 2 Moderate Use, Option 3 Strict Use.

units.why: Option 1 says "students are encouraged to use Generative AI Tools such as ChatGPT", a default of encouraging use, so P02 and encourage.
units.anchor: students are encouraged to use Generative AI Tools such as ChatGPT to support their work

units.why: "Students must give credit and cite any AI-generated material" requires attribution of AI output, so P24 with must (not P25, since no tool, prompt or date details are demanded here).
units.anchor: Students must give credit and cite any AI-generated material

units.why: Option 1 requires an acknowledgement statement naming the tool and purpose ("Students must also include the following statement in assignments"), a per-submission disclosure, so P24 (the tool name is only part of a statement, not a detailed citation as in P25).
units.anchor: Students must also include the following statement in assignments
units.frag_start: Students must also include the following
units.policy: Students must include an acknowledgement statement naming the Generative AI Tool and its purpose in assignments to indicate use.

units.why: Option 2 says students "are permitted to use Generative AI tools such as ChatGPT for specific assignments, as designated by the instructor", so the instructor decides assignment by assignment, which fits P04 better than P02 because permission is not by default.
units.anchor: permitted to use Generative AI tools such as ChatGPT for specific assignments
units.frag_start: students are permitted to use Generative AI tools

units.why: Option 2 asks for citation "according to [APA, MLA, etc.] rules", a citation-format requirement for AI material, so P24 with must; it differs from the Option 1 wording because it names a style guide.
units.anchor: cite any AI-generated material according to [APA, MLA, etc.] rules
units.frag_start: Students must give credit and cite any AI-generated material according

units.why: "Submitted work may be filtered through an AI Writing Detection tool" says detection software may be used on submissions, so P40 (the text does not say detectors are unreliable, which would be P39). It appears in Options 2 and 3 and is coded once.
units.anchor: Submitted work may be filtered through an AI Writing Detection tool.

units.why: "This review may initiate further discussion about the authenticity of the submission" means a conversation about the work follows the detector review, before any formal step, which matches P57.
units.anchor: further discussion about the authenticity of the submission
units.frag_start: This review may initiate further discussion

units.why: The review "could result in a more formal review through the Honor Code Council", which sends suspected misuse to the integrity process, so P36 with may.
units.anchor: a more formal review through the Honor Code Council
units.frag_start: This review may initiate further discussion

units.why: Option 3 states "it is expected that all submitted work is produced by students themselves", an ownership expectation of submitted work, so P29 with should.
units.anchor: it is expected that all submitted work is produced by students themselves

units.why: "Use of a Generative AI tool to complete an assignment" is treated as dishonest in the strict option; this is the ban on having AI produce submitted work, so P19 with must-not.
units.anchor: Use of a Generative AI tool to complete an assignment constitutes academic dishonesty
units.frag_start: Use of a Generative AI tool
units.policy: Use of a Generative AI tool to complete an assignment is not allowed.

units.why: Such use "will be reported as an Honor Code Violation", classifying it as misconduct handled by the Honor Code process, so P36 with must (the report is required); this is separate from the ban unit above.
units.anchor: will be reported as an Honor Code Violation
units.frag_start: Use of a Generative AI tool

notes: Only two included documents; both coded in full. Option 1 acknowledgement statement and the shared detection sentence were coded once to avoid repeats.
